title: Hamburger on wheat bun, 1 small patty

content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger on a wheat bun with one small beef patty (1701) is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a soft bun, juicy patty, lettuce leaf, tomato slice, pickles and sauce. It is often served with fries and a drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hamburger was served in the United States in the late 19th century.
A wheat bun gives a softer texture compared with traditional rye buns.
The patty weighs about 50 g, making it “small” compared with standard burger patties.
The hamburger is a symbol of American culture and is popular worldwide.
There are countless topping variations: cheese, bacon, avocado, various sauces.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hamburgers contain vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: The wheat bun supplies complex carbohydrates that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If the bun is whole‑grain, it adds fiber that benefits digestion.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: A hamburger can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Sauces and processed ingredients may increase salt intake, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked patty may harbor pathogens such as E. coli.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hamburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding them with both hands. Add cheese, bacon, sauces, and fresh vegetables to suit your taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared hamburger in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours in an airtight container. For longer storage, separate the components: the bun can be frozen, and the patty can be kept in the freezer for up to 3 months.
